compute.reported_as: Appendix C: We note that the training of our ansatz was performed using P100 GPUs. In order to produce the results of Fig. 3(b), we use d_h = 300 and N_s = 100 samples for training. We have first performed annealing on the system size 6 x 6 with N_warmup = 1000, N_annealing = 10000, and an initial pseudo-temperature T_0 = 0.25, while using a fixed learning rate eta = 5 x 10^-4. During each annealing step, we perform N_train = 5 gradient descent steps. In this initial phase, we only apply the U(1) symmetry. In the next phase, we perform an additional 25000 gradients steps at zero pseudo-temperature and add an additional 25000 gradients steps after applying C2d symmetry. [...] We then increase the system size to 8 x 8, while keeping our ansatz parameters fixed, applying C2d symmetry and while using zero pseudo-temperature. In this phase, the learning rate is fixed to eta = 10^-5. After this step, we train our RNN ansatz until convergence. We repeat the same procedure for system sizes 10 x 10, 12 x 12, 14 x 14 and 16 x 16. We note that for 8 x 8, we add 40000 gradient steps. For 10 x 10, we continue training with 20000 gradient steps. For 12 x 12, we converge using 10000 training steps. For 14 x 14, we continue training with 5000 gradient steps. Finally, for 16 x 16, we add 2000 convergence steps. || Sec. 3.2: Interestingly, our RNN ansatz uses less than 0.1% of the parameters of DMRG for system sizes larger than 14 x 14. || Checklist 3(d): [...] the total amount of compute was not included due to the lack of data.
